venue.name: TLC The Land Conservancy of British Columbia
venue.description: TLC The Land Conservancy of British Columbia is a non profit, charitable land trust founded in 1997 and run from a head office at 5150 Cordova Bay Road in Victoria. It protects habitat for plants, animals and natural communities as well as properties with historical, cultural, scientific or scenic value, and it holds conservation covenants across the province. What it offers the public directly is an annual event series called Passport to Nature, mostly free and held at sites around B.C. or online, plus a multiday naturalist workshop for adults and a free online library of printable nature activity sheets for teachers and caregivers. The head office itself is an office, not a visitor site, and TLC also operates Abkhazi Garden in Victoria, which is listed separately.
venue.address: 5150 Cordova Bay Road, Victoria, B.C. V8Y 2K6
venue.hours_notes: The office answers the phone Tuesday to Friday on 250-479-8053 or toll free 1-877-485-2422.
venue.seasonal_notes: Passport to Nature runs as an annual series of dated events spread through the year. The 2026 events listed at the time of checking were 13 September, 17 October, 7 November and 12 to 20 December.

programs.name: Passport to Nature events
programs.description: An annual series of dated nature events run by TLC at sites across British Columbia, including TLC protected areas that are normally closed to the public, plus some online sessions. Sessions are led by TLC staff and board, local nature experts and naturalists, and cover things like ecological restoration, plant and fungi identification and pollinator friendly gardening. Registration is free unless the listing says otherwise, and is required for events that have a cap on numbers. The events are described as family friendly and as catering to a wide range of abilities, though some are more physically demanding than others, so each listing has to be read on its own. Events listed for autumn 2026 were a Fall Open House and plant sale at Abkhazi Garden on 13 September, Ayum Creek Plant the Peninsula on 17 October, a Fungi ID Walk at John Dean Park on 7 November and a Festive Market from 12 to 20 December. A full season booklet is published as a PDF.
programs.what_children_do: Walk with a naturalist on land that is usually closed to the public, stop to look closely at plants and fungi and learn to name them, and at the restoration days pull invasive plants out or put young plants into the ground.
programs.our_note: These are single dated events on a public calendar rather than something you can book for a class on a day that suits you, so watch the calendar and register early where numbers are capped. No age range is published and the events are scattered across the province, so check the location and what the walking is like before you sign up a group.
programs.practical_summary: Most events are free, some run online and the rest happen at TLC sites around B.C. rather than at one address. Nothing is published about washrooms, lunch space, ages or how many adults have to come, so ask when you register.
programs.extra_fees_note: Registration is free unless an individual event says otherwise.
programs.cancellation_note: Please register in advance to secure your spot and let us know if you can no longer attend so that we can give your spot to someone on the waitlist.
programs.evidence: Unless otherwise indicated, registration for Passport to Nature events is FREE.

programs.name: Deertrails Naturalist Program
programs.description: A multiday naturalist workshop for adults only, described as being for students, teachers, artists and naturalists. The 2026 workshop ran from Friday 21 August to Monday 24 August at Linnaea Farm on Cortes Island, and registration for it has closed. Sessions include a lichen and fungi walk, mobile nature photography, place based writing and a wetland restoration circle. The base fee covers instruction and meals; accommodation is added on top at $60 per person per night in the farmhouse or $25 per person per night to camp. Bursaries cover up to half the workshop fee for people who need financial help. Participants arrange their own travel, which means two ferries by way of Quadra Island. No dogs or other pets are permitted. Walks are on moderately difficult uneven forest ground with hills, and participants should expect to walk up to 5km and be away from washrooms for up to four hours at a time.
programs.our_note: This one is for grown ups only, 19 and over, so treat it as staff development rather than a field trip. It is on Cortes Island by two ferries and registration for 2026 has already closed, so the useful move is to ask to go on the mailing list for the next one.
programs.practical_summary: Meals are included and beds or a tent pitch cost extra, and there are plumbed washrooms and showers at the farmhouse. The base fee itself is not published on the page, and you get to Cortes Island under your own steam on two ferries.
programs.extra_fees_note: The base workshop fee is not published on the page. Accommodation is added on top: farmhouse stay $60 per person per night, or camping $25 per person per night. An advance check in the night before costs $60 or $25 per person. Bursaries cover up to 50 per cent of the workshop fee.
programs.payment_timing: Participants should expect to pay course fees within the week after their registration is confirmed.
programs.cancellation_note: We will fully reimburse program fees for any participants needing to cancel.
programs.evidence: Deertrails is intended for adult (19+) participants only.

images.alt: A narrow footpath with a few stone steps leads up into a sunlit conifer forest with ferns and green undergrowth.
Four people carrying day packs walk in single file along a narrow trail through a mossy forest of tall thin trees.

gaps: TLC operates Abkhazi Garden in Victoria, which is already in this catalog as its own entry. Nothing from the Abkhazi Garden pages was copied here. If a director wants a garden visit, the Abkhazi Garden record is the one to read.

No school programs, class visits, guided group tours or outreach visits are published anywhere on the TLC site. Passport to Nature events are public dated events open to individuals and families, not bookings a group can make on its own date.
AGES: no age range or minimum age is published for Passport to Nature. The only stated age rule on the site is that Deertrails is 19 and over.
PRICE: Passport to Nature registration is free unless a listing says otherwise, but the base fee for the Deertrails workshop is not published on the page.
CAPACITY: the site says some events have attendance maximums but never says what they are.
LEAD TIME: no minimum notice is published for registering for an event.

The head office address is an office and mailing address. Passport to Nature events happen at TLC sites all over British Columbia rather than at that address, so the pin for this record is the office, not a place to take children.
Washrooms, lunch space, rain backup, wheelchair and stroller access and bus parking are not addressed anywhere for TLC as an organisation.
No coordinates are published on the site, so the address was captured and the map pin is left for a later pass.

The Education Hub is a free library of printable activity books, bird and intertidal bingo sheets, colouring pages and a free scavenger hunt app for teachers and caregivers. It is a download library rather than a visit, so it was not recorded as a program.
The site's social preview picture is a collage of Abkhazi Garden, which is a separate entry here, so the forest path photograph from the home page was used as the main picture instead.
The Passport to Nature season booklet and the Visitor's Guide are hosted as PDFs, one of them on an outside file sharing service. Neither was read.
Volunteer restoration days are advertised for adults and give no age rule, so they were not recorded as a children's offering.

Two general email addresses are published. The contact page (last updated February 2026) gives HOAdmin@conservancy.bc.ca for general inquiries, while the banner on every page gives admin@conservancy.bc.ca. The contact page value was recorded.

conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different general email addresses. If one bounces, try the other. We use the one from their contact page.
